analysis: Examined: docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md head 284-659 (only changes: date line 3 and tenant-partition row line 621 adding Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix.scopes); Package.swift (TensorParallelCheck now depends on DarkbloomClusterQualification, a no-MLX qualification target; qualification tool only, not worker product); NativeWorkerRuntime.swift new .gemma4TensorParallel owner case. Gemma dispatch (head 37-45) is selected before the Qwen TP case when family==.qwenDense, mode tensorParallel and Gemma4TensorParallelResidentRuntime.serves(modelID). It requires no speculation/assistant policy, shares [1,1] and a non-nil dataPlane (keyed data plane), and passes prefixSSDKey, consistent with other TP runtimes. All lifecycle forwards (reserve/start/release/cancel/lane ops/shutdown/ping) are mechanical. releaseIdleMemory delegates to the runtime with try? (failure returns nil, same pattern as GLM). refreshServingContext returns nil for Gemma. No regression identified locally. Relevant threats: T-041/SEC-035 (prefix-cache tenant scoping, at-rest SSD records), TB-007. Integration questions (source not supplied): Gemma4TensorParallelResidentRuntime.load and Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix.scopes must fold the tenant salt digest into record scope and honor 'disabled' (no offer/restore/write) as the doc claims; its SSD tier must use the owner-derived key with DBPXSSD1 sealing and per-rank directories; serves(runtimeModelID:) must be an exact model-ID match so a non-Gemma Qwen ID cannot be misrouted; whether prefixSSDKey nil disables the SSD tier rather than falling back to an unkeyed store; capturesLogprobs and memory-pressure prefix eviction behavior. These are unverified contracts, not findings.
